title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: Product trending on TikTok with no prior history; noise-adjusted effect of similar drivers is x1.10, but evidence is thin (one occurrence).

drivers.name: Price increase
drivers.evidence: Price increased 4.1% above regular; past price hikes show no consistent lift (noise-adjusted x1.02), and no prior 4%+ increase seen. No evidence of demand sensitivity.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 25.1. Halloween (event week) has a noise-adjusted effect of x1.0, so no adjustment. The price increase to $13.93 (+4.1%) is above the historical average (13.38), and past price hikes show a median lift of x1.02, but this is a new, deeper price increase with no past parallel. The product is trending on TikTok, which may drive demand, but this is a single, untested driver. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but judgment overrides: a new viral trend with a price increase warrants a cautious upward adjustment. Evidence is thin, so shrink toward 1.0. Use x1.10 as a conservative, noise-adjusted estimate.

This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
